2005-2006-niger-food-crisis.name: 2005–06 Niger Food Crisis
2005-2006-niger-food-crisis.summary: Severe food security crisis in parts of Niger from 2005 to 2006, caused by drought, locust damage and chronic poverty, leaving over 800,000 people in extreme food insecurity.

2010-sahel-famine.name: 2010 Sahel Famine
2010-sahel-famine.summary: Drought-induced famine across Africa's Sahel region and nearby areas from February to August 2010, one of several recent famines to hit the zone.

jollof-rice.name: Jollof rice
jollof-rice.summary: West African rice dish originating in Senegal, typically cooked in a single pot with tomatoes, chilis, onions and spices; regional variants spark friendly rivalry across the region.

wolof-people.name: Wolof
wolof-people.summary: A Niger-Congo ethnic group native to the Senegambia region of West Africa and the largest ethnic group in Senegal, historically tied to the medieval Wolof Empire.

kenkey.name: Kenkey
kenkey.summary: A staple fermented dumpling-like food from the Ga and Fante regions of West Africa, typically served with pepper sauce, fried fish, soup or stew.

dambou.name: Dambou
dambou.summary: A dish of the Zarma and Songhai peoples of Niger made from cereals and moringa leaves, traditionally eaten at festive occasions like weddings.

chakery.name: Chakery
chakery.summary: A sweet West African dessert of millet couscous mixed with milk or yogurt and dried fruit, first recorded among the Fulani of northern Senegal before spreading across the region.

zobo-drink.name: Zobo
zobo-drink.summary: A tea made from the hibiscus plant roselle, popular in West Africa (called zobo in Nigeria, sobolo in Ghana) and usually drunk cold with fruits and spices added.

great-mosque-of-djenn.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
great-mosque-of-djenn.summary: The largest adobe brick building in the world, in Djenné, Mali; first built around the 13th century, with the current structure dating from 1907.

eweka-ii.name: Eweka II
eweka-ii.summary: Oba (king) of Benin from 1914 to 1933, son of the deposed Ovonramwen, who rebuilt the royal palace and craft guilds destroyed by the British in 1897, and under whom his father's seized royal regalia was returned.

akenzua-ii.name: Akenzua II
akenzua-ii.summary: The thirty-seventh Oba of Benin, reigning from 1933 until his death in 1978 (1899–1978).

benin-bronzes.name: Benin Bronzes
benin-bronzes.summary: Thousands of metal plaques and sculptures that decorated the royal palace of the Kingdom of Benin, mostly taken by British forces during the 1897 Benin Expedition.

museum-of-west-african-art.name: Museum of West African Art
museum-of-west-african-art.summary: Museum built in Benin City, Nigeria, designed by architect David Adjaye, meant to focus on contemporary West African art, its opening delayed by protests in 2025.

david-adjaye.name: David Adjaye
david-adjaye.summary: A Ghanaian-British architect, knighted in 2017, who has designed notable buildings worldwide including the National Museum of African American History and Culture in Washington, D.C.

benin-city.name: Benin City
benin-city.summary: Today the capital of Edo State in southern Nigeria and Nigeria's fourth-largest city, historically the seat of the Oba's palace.

agadez.name: Agadez
agadez.summary: The fifth-largest city in Niger and capital of the Sultanate of Agadez, a traditional Tuareg-Berber federation; its historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

ekpo-eyo.name: Ekpo Eyo
ekpo-eyo.summary: A Nigerian scholar (1931–2011) who worked across archaeology, anthropology and art history and long presided over Nigeria's national antiquities and museums agencies.

kingdom-of-benin.name: Kingdom of Benin
kingdom-of-benin.summary: A long-lived kingdom in what is now southern Nigeria, centered on Benin City, renowned by the 15th–16th centuries for trade with Europe and for its bronze, ivory and brass artistry, before British annexation in 1897.

national-museum-of-african-art.name: Smithsonian Museum of African Art
national-museum-of-african-art.summary: The Smithsonian Institution's African art museum on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., the first U.S. museum dedicated to African art, founded in 1964 and joined to the Smithsonian in 1979.

nok-culture.name: Nok culture
nok-culture.summary: An ancient population in what is now Nigeria, named for the village where its terracotta sculptures were first found in 1928, existing from roughly 1500 BCE to 1 CE.

kaduna-state.name: Kaduna State
kaduna-state.summary: State in northwest Nigeria home to the Nok civilization (c. 1500 BC to 500 AD) and later part of the Sokoto Caliphate; became capital of the British Northern Nigeria Protectorate.

yakubu-gowon.name: Yakubu Gowon
yakubu-gowon.summary: Nigerian general who served as military head of state from 1966 to 1975 and led the country through the Nigerian Civil War (Biafra War).

nigerian-national-museum.name: Nigerian National Museum
nigerian-national-museum.summary: National museum of Nigeria in Lagos, holding Nigerian art, carvings, and archaeological and ethnographic exhibits; reopened in 2026 after a major renovation.

elizabeth-ii.name: Elizabeth II
elizabeth-ii.summary: Queen of the United Kingdom and Commonwealth realms from 1952 until her death in 2022, reigning for 70 years, the longest of any British monarch.

royal-collection.name: Royal Collection
royal-collection.summary: The world's largest private art collection, owned by the British monarch and spread across 13 royal residences, holding more than a million objects including paintings, jewellery and manuscripts.

geography-of-ghana.name: Volta Basin
geography-of-ghana.summary: A region taking up most of south-central Ghana, drained by tributary rivers such as the Oti and Afram that feed Lake Volta, the world's largest artificial lake.

west-african-cfa-franc.name: West African CFA franc
west-african-cfa-franc.summary: The shared currency of eight West African states, issued since 1945 by the Central Bank of West African States and produced by the Bank of France.

al-qaeda-in-the-islamic-maghreb.name: Al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb (AQIM)
al-qaeda-in-the-islamic-maghreb.summary: An al-Qaeda-linked Islamist militant organization active in North Africa's Maghreb and Sahel regions, known for kidnapping for ransom, that grew out of an Algerian insurgent group.

operation-barkhane.name: Operation Barkhane
operation-barkhane.summary: French-led counterinsurgency operation (2014–2022) against Islamist groups across the Sahel, involving Burkina Faso, Chad, Mali, Mauritania and Niger, headquartered in N'Djamena, Chad.

battle-of-dakar.name: Battle of Dakar
battle-of-dakar.summary: An unsuccessful 1940 Allied operation to seize the port of Dakar in French West Africa and replace its pro-German Vichy administration with a Free French one under Charles de Gaulle.

charles-de-gaulle.name: Charles de Gaulle
charles-de-gaulle.summary: French general and statesman (1890–1970) who led the Free French Forces in World War II and later served as President of France from 1958 to 1969.

vichy-france.name: Vichy France
vichy-france.summary: The French state headed by Marshal Pétain from 1940 to 1944, formed after Germany's victory over France and based in the town of Vichy in the unoccupied 'free zone.'

french-west-africa.name: French West Africa
french-west-africa.summary: A federation of eight French colonial territories in West Africa, eight times the size of mainland France, that existed from 1895 to 1958 with its capital at Dakar.

french-equatorial-africa.name: French Equatorial Africa
french-equatorial-africa.summary: A federation of French colonial territories comprising Gabon, French Congo, Ubangi-Shari and Chad, administered from Brazzaville from 1910 to 1958.

troupes-coloniales.name: Troupes coloniales
troupes-coloniales.summary: The colonial troops of the French colonial empire from 1900 to 1961, recruited from mainland France, settlers, and indigenous populations, who fought in the empire's conquest and both World Wars.

french-battleship-richelieu.name: Richelieu
french-battleship-richelieu.summary: A French fast battleship launched in 1939, damaged in British attacks at Dakar in 1940 before later joining the Free French Naval Forces.

hms-barham-04.name: HMS Barham
hms-barham-04.summary: A Queen Elizabeth-class Royal Navy battleship completed in 1915, which fought in both World Wars before being sunk off Egypt in 1941 with the loss of 862 crew.

ajami-script.name: Ajami script
ajami-script.summary: An Arabic-derived script adapted to write African languages such as Hausa, Fula and Swahili, using extra dots or marks rather than new letters for sounds Arabic lacks.

french-sudan.name: French Sudan
french-sudan.summary: A French colonial territory in West Africa from around 1880 that became the independent Republic of Mali in 1960.

ansar-dine.name: Ansar Dine
ansar-dine.summary: A Sunni Islamist militant group led by Iyad Ag Ghaly that sought to impose sharia across Mali, seizing Timbuktu in 2012 before merging into another group in 2017.

mali-war.name: Mali War
mali-war.summary: Ongoing conflict beginning in 2012 with a Tuareg rebellion in northern Mali, during which Islamist rebels captured Timbuktu, Kidal and Gao.

henry-louis-gates-jr.name: Henry Louis Gates Jr.
henry-louis-gates-jr.summary: American literary critic, historian and Harvard professor who has hosted the PBS series Finding Your Roots and rediscovered early African-American novels.

kwame-nkrumah.name: Kwame Nkrumah
kwame-nkrumah.summary: Ghanaian politician (1909–1972) who led the Gold Coast to independence in 1957 as its first prime minister, then served as Ghana's first president until 1966, and championed Pan-Africanism.

zola-maseko.name: Zola Maseko
zola-maseko.summary: Swazi film director and screenwriter, born in 1967, known for documentary films about xenophobia.

dhar-tichitt.name: Dhar Tichitt
dhar-tichitt.summary: A line of sandstone cliffs in southwestern Mauritania with Neolithic sites inhabited by pastoralists and farmers between about 2000 and 300 BCE, among the oldest known settlements in West Africa.

soninke-people.name: Soninke
soninke-people.summary: A West African Mande-speaking ethnic group who founded the ancient empire of Ghana (Wagadou), around 200 to 1240 CE, later spreading widely as traders.

koumbi-saleh.name: Koumbi Saleh
koumbi-saleh.summary: A ruined ancient and medieval city site in southeast Mauritania, long thought to be the capital of the Ghana Empire, occupied roughly from the 5th to 14th centuries.

san-mali.name: San
san-mali.summary: A town in the Ségou Region of Mali, on the Bani River, with about 68,000 residents as of 2009.

global-innovation-index.name: Global Innovation Index
global-innovation-index.summary: An annual ranking of countries by their capacity for innovation, published since 2007 by the World Intellectual Property Organization using data from sources such as the World Bank.

djenn.name: Djenné
djenn.summary: Historic town in central Mali closely tied to Timbuktu through trans-Saharan trade in salt, gold and slaves, famed for its adobe Sudano-Sahelian architecture.

african-union-development-agency.name: New Partnership for Africa's Development
african-union-development-agency.summary: An African Union economic development program, adopted in 2001 in Lusaka, providing a policy framework to accelerate economic cooperation and integration among African countries.

french-guinea.name: French Guinea
french-guinea.summary: A French colonial possession in West Africa established in 1891, corresponding by 1958 to the borders of present-day Guinea.

french-upper-volta.name: Upper Volta
french-upper-volta.summary: A French West African colony established in 1919 covering present-day Burkina Faso, named for the upper Volta River, which gained independence in 1960.

french-dahomey.name: Dahomey
french-dahomey.summary: A French colony in West Africa from 1894 to 1958, part of French West Africa, which gained independence in 1960 and was renamed Benin in 1975.

ghana-empire.name: Ghana Empire
ghana-empire.summary: An ancient West African empire based in what is now southeast Mauritania and western Mali, first mentioned in writing in 830 CE; it became a vassal of the Mali Empire in the 13th century.

gold-coast-british-colony.name: Gold Coast (British colony)
gold-coast-british-colony.summary: British Crown colony on West Africa's Gulf of Guinea coast, 1821 to 1957, named for the region's gold and later becoming independent Ghana.

bambara-language.name: Bambara
bambara-language.summary: A lingua franca and national language of Mali, spoken natively by about 4.2 million Bambara people and as a second language by roughly 10 million more, with about 80% of Malians speaking it.

loi-cadre-defferre.name: Loi-cadre Defferre
loi-cadre-defferre.summary: A 1956 French legal reform, named after minister Gaston Defferre, that transferred powers to elected governments in French African colonies and introduced universal suffrage.

ecowas.name: ECOWAS
ecowas.summary: A regional political and economic union of twelve West African countries, established in 1975 to promote economic integration, free movement of people and shared development.

mali-federation.name: Mali Federation
mali-federation.summary: Short-lived 1959-1960 union of French Senegal and the Sudanese Republic, which collapsed after two months, leading the Sudanese Republic to rename itself Mali.

conseil-de-l-entente.name: Conseil de l'Entente
conseil-de-l-entente.summary: A West African regional cooperation forum established in 1959 by Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Upper Volta, and Dahomey, grown out of the earlier Sahel-Benin Union.

conakry.name: Conakry
conakry.summary: The capital and largest city of Guinea, and the country's economic, financial and cultural centre, with a 2025 population of about 3.4 million.

akan-philosophy.name: Akan philosophy
akan-philosophy.summary: A branch of African philosophy from the Akan people of West Africa, notably shaping modern debate on personhood as something achieved by degrees, as argued by philosopher Kwasi Wiredu.

kwasi-wiredu.name: Kwasi Wiredu
kwasi-wiredu.summary: Ghanaian philosopher (1931–2022) often called the greatest African philosopher of his generation, known for work on the conceptual decolonisation of African thought.

timbuktu-manuscripts.name: Timbuktu Manuscripts
timbuktu-manuscripts.summary: Centuries-old manuscripts on art, medicine, philosophy, science and the Quran, preserved in private homes in Timbuktu, Mali, mostly written in Arabic.

songhay-languages.name: Songhay
songhay-languages.summary: A group of closely related West African languages spoken along the Niger River, used for centuries as a lingua franca since the era of the Songhai Empire.

charlie-english-writer.name: Charlie English
charlie-english-writer.summary: A British writer and journalist born in 1967, formerly head of international news at The Guardian, who has written four acclaimed non-fiction books.

akan-people.name: Akan people
akan-people.summary: A Kwa-speaking people of Ghana and Ivory Coast made up of subgroups such as the Asante and Fante, traditionally tracing royal descent through the mother's line.

mand-peoples.name: Mandé peoples
mand-peoples.summary: A broader grouping of West African peoples, including the Mandinka, who speak related Mande languages and share a common caste system, predominantly Muslim today.

kanuri-people.name: Kanuri
kanuri-people.summary: An African ethnic group living mainly in the lands of the former Kanem and Bornu Empires across Niger, Nigeria, Chad, and Cameroon, traditionally sedentary farmers, fishers, and traders.

zarma-people.name: Zarma people
zarma-people.summary: An ethnic group mainly in western Niger, also found in Nigeria and Benin, closely related to but historically distinct from the neighboring Songhai; predominantly Muslim herders of the Niger River valley.

oware.name: Oware
oware.summary: A mancala board game believed to be of Ashanti origin, played across West Africa and the Caribbean under many local names.

goethe-university-frankfurt.name: Goethe University Frankfurt
goethe-university-frankfurt.summary: A public research university in Frankfurt, Germany, founded in 1914 and renamed for Johann Wolfgang von Goethe in 1932, with 20 Nobel Prize winners affiliated.

national-commission-for-museums-and-monu.name: National Commission for Museums and Monuments
national-commission-for-museums-and-monu.summary: Nigeria's federal body, founded in 1979, responsible for collecting, documenting and presenting the country's cultural heritage to the public.
national-commission-for-museums-and-monu.source_title: National Commission for Museums and Monuments

kaabu.name: Kaabu
kaabu.summary: Federation of Mandinka kingdoms (1537-1867) in the Senegambia region, originally a military province of the Mali Empire; its capital Kansala fell to Fula forces in 1867.

nyancho.name: Nyancho
nyancho.summary: The royal maternal dynasty that ruled the West African empire of Kaabu.
